#### 1. autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2T  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.481)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-446205)

**Proposed mechanism:** Loss-of-function variants in MPI —DISRUPTS→ MPI (HGNC:7301); MPI (HGNC:7301) —DECREASES→ Mannose metabolism (REACT:REACT-169811); Mannose metabolism (REACT:REACT-169811) —LEADS_TO→ Congenital disorder of glycosylation type I (MONDO:0011257); Loss-of-function variants in GMPPB —DISRUPTS→ GMPPB (HGNC:27907); GMPPB (HGNC:27907) —DECREASES→ Protein O-linked glycosylation pathway (GO:0006494); Protein O-linked glycosylation pathway (GO:0006494) —LEADS_TO→ Autosomal recessive limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2T (MONDO:0014142); Mannose metabolism (REACT:REACT-169811) —BINDS→ Protein O-linked glycosylation pathway (GO:0006494). Loss-of-function mutations in MPI disrupt mannose metabolism, impacting protein glycosylation, leading to MONDO:0011257. Similarly, loss-of-function mutations in GMPPB impair the protein O-linked glycosylation pathway, causing MONDO:0014142. Both pathways converge on the general process of protein glycosylation, highlighting a shared mechanistic basis.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of homozygous or hemizygous pathogenic variants in MPI or GMPPB in individuals diagnosed with the other disease would falsify this hypothesis. Furthermore, if genetic analysis reveals that the primary defect in one of the diseases does not involve the glycosylation pathway, this hypothesis would be weakened. _(variant: A pathogenic variant in MPI or GMPPB with a gnomAD allele frequency > 0.01 would suggest it is not disease-specific.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of protein glycosylation in both MONDO:0011257 and MONDO:0014142 could lead to the development of therapies targeting this pathway, potentially benefiting patients with either condition. For instance, therapies aimed at improving general protein folding or stability might offer a common therapeutic avenue.
